extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers for ESA journals (Ecology, Ecological Monographs, Ecological Applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for reviewers evaluating manuscripts submitted to Ecology, Ecological Monographs, and Ecological Applications, covering confidentiality, conflicts of interest, open research expectations, fairness/anonymity, and detailed guidance on what to assess and report (presentation, methods, data/code, statistics, citations, overlap, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Each manuscript is a privileged communication; reviewers should not show or discuss a manuscript with anyone else except to solicit assistance with a technical point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you think a colleague is more qualified, request permission from editorial staff before passing the manuscript on. The review and recommendation are confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship (Joint Review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Encouragement and procedure for involving graduate students or postdocs in reviews as joint reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request editorial staff add the mentee as a reviewer with name and email. All participants can submit the same review and get credit. Each reviewer must submit their own copy of the review so the Subject Matter Editor receives all reviews; coordinate due dates. Joint reviewers need not submit identical reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: If you might have difficulty writing an objective review or have (or could be construed to have) connections with authors/institutions that create a conflict, alert editorial staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no actual conflict exists but a previous/present connection might be construed as one, discuss it in confidential comments to the editor. When in doubt, contact esajournals@esa.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Research Policy — reviewer expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: ESA's Open Research Policy aims to support reproducibility and transparency; reviewers are not expected to enforce every part but should consider specific items during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether novel code has been provided as supporting information (authors are required to submit novel code); note missing novel code in your review. Check for discrepancies in data presentation (e.g., whether the proposed data statement will provide necessary underlying data or if additional material is needed). Reviewers are not expected to fully examine linked data in detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness and objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticize the science, not the scientist; reviews should be objective, respectful, and intended to help authors improve manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid harsh words that undermine perceived objectivity. Ensure criticisms are not merely differences of opinion and are clearly correct and constructive. Aim to win the author's respect and appreciation for the effort to be effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer qualifications and evidence of careful reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should convince the author that you have read the entire manuscript carefully and are qualified to provide an expert opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that your criticisms are objective and correct (not mere opinion). If you cannot provide an expert, decline or note limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may sign reviews or remain anonymous; if anonymous, avoid comments that reveal identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you choose anonymity, avoid remarks or annotations that might serve as clues to your identity. Unless you indicate otherwise, the journal assumes you wish to remain anonymous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments for the Author — overall assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the manuscript's major contributions, strengths, weaknesses, and whether it is suitable for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both general and specific comments and emphasize the most significant points.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Comments — topics to address
rubrics_metrics.description: General Comments should address importance/interest to the journal's readers; scientific soundness; originality; degree to which conclusions are supported; organization and clarity; cohesiveness of argument; length vs information content; whether material should be moved to digital appendices; conciseness and writing style; and appropriateness for the targeted journal/section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover these topics in your General Comments to give editors and authors a clear sense of the manuscript's fit and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the manuscript tells a cohesive story and whether a tightly reasoned argument is evident throughout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify where the manuscript wanders from the argument. Check that title, abstract, keywords, introduction, and conclusions accurately and consistently reflect the major point(s). Judge whether the writing is concise, easy to follow, and interesting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length (specificity requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate which portions should be expanded, condensed, combined, or deleted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about what to change; do not advise an overall shortening by X%—give precise suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — appropriateness and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether methods are appropriate, current, and described clearly enough for someone else to repeat the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request additional methodological detail if necessary for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and/or code presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether results stated in the text can be verified from tables/figures, whether any results are counterintuitive, and whether tables/figures are necessary, clearly labeled, well planned, and readily interpretable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that any provided data are presented so a reader can replicate results. Confirm that authors have provided novel code required to replicate analyses and flag missing code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical design and analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether statistical design and analyses are appropriate and correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check which measurements/observations are independent, that replicates are correctly identified, and whether significance statements are justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errors (technique, fact, calculation, interpretation, style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Point out any errors in technique, fact, calculation, interpretation, or style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag technical mistakes and stylistic issues. Note that the journal follows ASTM Standard E380‑93 for use of SI units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether all pertinent references are cited and whether any citations are irrelevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure citations are provided for assertions of fact not supported by the manuscript's data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlap / originality relative to existing literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the manuscript reports data or conclusions that are already published or in press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If overlap exists, provide details (e.g., citations, what is duplicated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review submission protocol and editorial-only materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural requirements for submitting reviews and for uploading files visible only to the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all required review-form fields (marked by a red “*”) are completed before submission. To upload a file only the Editor will see, select 'For Editor Only' when uploading; if you cannot submit, save a PDF copy of your review and contact esajournals@esa.org.
